title: URL reconstruction preserves string or byte representation
answers: Why does a reconstructed byte URL contain b'...' notation?
How do I build a URL from byte components?
body:
Symptom: Reconstructing a URL from byte components produces Python byte-literal notation instead of a usable byte URL.
Root cause: mitmproxy/net/http/url.py:unparse used string interpolation for byte components.
Fix pattern: Select string or byte construction based on the scheme type, preserving the corresponding return type; test/mitmproxy/net/http/test_url.py:test_unparse covers byte reconstruction.
Constraints: Use consistently typed string or byte components and supply an explicit path; the overloads do not promise support for mixed representations.
applies: Calls to url.unparse that reconstruct URLs from string or byte components.
